title: PBS DMS vs Clearline: how the DMS, CRM and AI workflows fit
summary: Need a PBS alternative? Compare PBS DMS and Clearline. Keep PBS for operations; add AI to answer calls, follow up, and book service appointments in PBS.
body_markdown:
If you are looking for a PBS DMS alternative, start with the failure you want to fix. Are accounting, parts, deal processing, or service operations the problem? That calls for a DMS evaluation. Or do customers call after hours, submit leads that sit untouched, and ask to book while no one is available? Those are conversation and execution problems.


PBS Systems and Clearline address different parts of that picture. PBS is the dealership's operating system. Clearline answers and follows up with customers, then completes supported actions in connected systems. The useful comparison is where they overlap, where they connect, and which result your store needs to improve.


## What PBS dealership software does


[PBS v10 APEX](https://www.pbssystems.com/dms) covers accounting, sales, service, parts, CRM, and its Digital Service Suite. PBS describes[accounting tools](https://www.pbssystems.com/accounting) for posting and invoicing, a built-in[sales lead module](https://www.pbssystems.com/sales) ,[parts inventory tools](https://www.pbssystems.com/parts) , and[service software](https://www.pbssystems.com/service) with online appointment booking and technician dispatch. The[PBS CRM](https://www.pbssystems.com/crm) supports customizable communication templates, predictive marketing that identifies vehicles due for service, and internal sales tasks.


That is a broad platform. A fair PBS Systems review should assess whether those workflows fit the store: whether staff can run the books, manage repair orders and parts, work leads, and see the schedule reliably. Clearline is not a substitute for any of those core DMS functions.


## Where Clearline fits alongside PBS DMS


Clearline's AI agent, Luna, handles customer conversations across calls, SMS, email follow-up, and website chat. Its[CRM](https://www.useclearline.com/product/crm) keeps the conversation, outcome, and next action visible in one record. A customer can ask a question, get an approved answer, and book an eligible visit during the same interaction. Staff can step in when judgment is needed.


The distinction is especially important in service. PBS already offers online booking. Clearline adds a way to complete a booking during a phone call, text exchange, or chat, with the confirmed PBS integration creating the **service appointment directly in PBS** . Clearline can also book a sales test drive through its scheduling workflow; ask which PBS records, if any, that workflow updates at your store.

## PBS CRM and Clearline CRM: where they overlap


PBS CRM already helps a dealership identify service opportunities, assign sales tasks, and send templated communications. Clearline's CRM is organized around the conversation: what the customer said across phone, text, email, and chat; what happened next; and who needs to act. Both systems may touch the same customer, so adding Clearline requires a clear owner for each workflow.


Take a due-service reminder. Decide where the audience comes from, which system sends the first message, who handles a reply, and where the confirmed booking appears. If PBS sends a template while Clearline runs a separate campaign to the same person, the customer may get duplicate outreach. The[dealership data and integrations hub](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/pillars/dealership-data-integrations) covers how to assign a source of truth and define which system can read or update each record.


## A PBS service booking, step by step


Consider a returning service customer who calls after the advisors have left. The customer wants an appointment and has a question about their vehicle. In a configured Clearline and PBS workflow:


1. [Luna answers](https://www.useclearline.com/product/inbound) and identifies the customer and request. The customer does not have to wait for a next-day voicemail callback.
2. Clearline retrieves the available customer and vehicle details, service history, and Workplan activity from PBS. It can use that context instead of making the customer start from scratch.
3. The conversation follows the store's approved appointment types, hours, required fields, and escalation rules. If the request is outside those rules, Clearline hands it to the service team with context.
4. For an eligible time the customer confirms, Clearline creates the service appointment in PBS and texts the confirmation. The service team sees the booking in the schedule it already manages.
5. The call transcript and summary are available in Clearline after the call, so a manager can review what the customer asked and how the booking was handled.


This is the practical difference between an integration that only displays a PBS logo and one that completes a service action in PBS. The[PBS integration announcement](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/clearline-pbs-systems-integration) documents the data used and the service appointment write-back. The exact booking path still depends on the dealership's PBS configuration and approved rules.


## Where the day-to-day difference shows up


### Calls and website inquiries get an answer


Luna can handle inbound sales, service, parts, and finance calls, including after hours, then book an eligible next step or route the caller to the right person.[AI web chat](https://www.useclearline.com/product/web-chat) can answer inventory, trade, finance, and service questions from connected dealership information, book a visit, and pass the full chat history to staff. If a visitor leaves a number but exits before booking, Clearline can continue by text. The operating gain is coverage at the moment a customer reaches out, rather than a new place to collect unanswered messages. Our guides to[after-hours calls](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/after-hours-calls-dealership) and[AI voice handoffs](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/how-ai-answers-phone-calls) go deeper on that workflow.


### Follow-up continues across channels


[Clearline campaigns](https://www.useclearline.com/product/campaigns) can work aged leads, untouched forms, lease maturities, lapsed service customers, recalls, and no-shows by phone, SMS, and email. The plan can run through day 90 by default and stops when a customer books, replies, or opts out. That matters when the store has lead lists but no dependable owner for the next contact.


In[Clearline's 2026 mystery shop of 53 Canadian dealerships](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/mystery-shop-dealership-lead-response-study-2026) , stores averaged 2.0 follow-up attempts over five days, and 28.3% never responded during the observation window. These are dealership response findings, not a measure of PBS performance. They show why a GM should audit the actual customer experience before assuming a DMS replacement will fix follow-up.


### Managers can see and control the work


Clearline summarizes calls, emails, texts, and web chats so the customer record carries preferences, recent contact, and a suggested next action. Managers and reps can watch Luna's SMS conversations as they happen and take over. Calls are transcribed after they end; this is not live call streaming. Staff can also ask questions about their own store in Clearline's dashboard, with the useful answers depending on connected data and permissions.


The dealership sets approved pricing and policy answers, hours, and handoff rules. Each inbox can run in Manual, Copilot, or Autopilot mode. Calls, texts, emails, and opt-outs are logged and reviewable in Clearline, giving managers a way to coach and correct the workflow. The[AI BDC vs human BDC guide](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/ai-bdc-vs-human-bdc) covers where people should remain involved.


## Do you need a PBS alternative or an AI layer?


**Evaluate another DMS** when the recurring problem is inside the core system: accounting controls, parts inventory, deal processing, repair-order workflow, dispatch, reporting, or data quality. Map the pain to the people who run that process and compare PBS against another DMS on those specific jobs.


**Evaluate an AI layer** when the customer-facing work is the bottleneck: unanswered calls, slow first response, follow-up that ends after one attempt, website chats that do not turn into visits, or bookings that staff re-enter by hand. PBS's[partner program](https://www.pbssystems.com/partners) offers API access and two-way data interfaces, which supports adding a tool around the DMS.


**If both are weak, make two decisions.** Replacing the DMS and fixing response coverage have different costs, owners, and success measures. A new DMS does not prove every lead will be contacted, and an AI agent does not repair an accounting or parts workflow.


Before deciding, inspect a week of calls and leads. Note who answered, how quickly a customer got a useful response, whether follow-up continued, and whether confirmed appointments appeared in PBS. Measure appointment set and show rates by department. That baseline tells you whether the first project should be DMS selection, conversation coverage, or both.


## Frequently asked questions


Is Clearline a PBS DMS alternative? +


No. Clearline handles conversations, follow-up, and booking. It does not replace PBS accounting, parts, deal processing, or other core DMS operations.


Does PBS already have a CRM and online booking? +


Yes. PBS describes a CRM with automated communications and service software with online appointment booking. Clearline adds AI conversations around those functions.


Does Clearline integrate with PBS? +


Yes. Clearline can use PBS customer, vehicle, service history, and Workplan context and create service appointments directly in PBS, subject to dealership configuration and rules.


Do Clearline sales appointments or CRM leads write into PBS? +


The public PBS integration announcement documents service appointment creation. Confirm sales and CRM write-back for your store in a demo.


Does Clearline work with other DMSs? +


Clearline connects with other dealership systems, but DMS support and available actions vary. Verify your store's read and write steps before rollout.
